## Zona Centro

We recommend spending a morning or day in the city center — ideally on a weekday, when it is
less crowded. Start at the [Zócalo](https://goo.gl/maps/Q45hTLR9pbUDxRik9) (the main plaza)
and walk to **Palacio Nacional** (the presidential office). You can walk in (bring a photo ID)
to see the Diego Rivera murals — really, really nice. The entrance is
[here](https://goo.gl/maps/oLVyi78eJjiKpV818). *(Update Feb 2023: you now need to
[book in advance via email](https://www.gob.mx/palacionacional/documentos/visita-palacio-nacional).)*
An optional side-trip is [Templo Mayor](https://goo.gl/maps/P3NpiWanQvsdXCum7), the Aztec ruins
in the middle of the city — or just grab a coffee [here](https://goo.gl/maps/RKQ6LjrpY32WAjwx9),
which has a nice terrace view of the ruins.

Next, stroll to [Bellas Artes](https://goo.gl/maps/XorSRvzZMakX5bJs5). Go into the building in
front (a [Sears](https://goo.gl/maps/XaYZNaVSeYD9hWvb6)) and head to the café on the 6th floor
for a gorgeous view of Bellas Artes and the Alameda. Walk around Alameda Central. If you want
more murals, visit this tiny [museum](https://goo.gl/maps/sAfttWmqev4AiVCC7) holding a single,
huge Diego Rivera mural.

If you still have energy, walk to the
[Monumento a la Revolución](https://goo.gl/maps/uvfHNE48ie48X2jN9) and/or Uber to the
[Museo de Antropología](https://goo.gl/maps/bZR6s2M4LpFDJRtk8). There, skip the history-of-humans
section and go straight to the pre-Hispanic (Aztec/Mayan) halls toward the back of the first
floor. From the museum it is a short walk into
[Bosque de Chapultepec](https://goo.gl/maps/uyTKe5SVWhYiyMWZ7), the biggest park in the city
(bigger than Central Park). We love the city view from the
[Castle](https://goo.gl/maps/CXkzdcNirgSxpRni9) (Museum of National History) and this
[fountain](https://goo.gl/maps/s8C32crL9zkrbVZY6).

**Food**

- Yucatán food, great cochinita pibil — [Coox Hanal](https://g.page/Cooxhanal?share)
- Mezcalería — [Bósforo](https://maps.app.goo.gl/ab28YpoQDnmU2yJe6) (next door there's a great restaurant with no name and no Google Maps listing)
- [Azul Histórico](https://maps.app.goo.gl/WyhddMPfDQEGvcGU7) — traditional Mexican food in a beautiful setting

## Zona Coyoacán / San Ángel

Another good day is exploring the colonial neighborhoods of San Ángel and Coyoacán (where the
intellectual elite lives — think Frida and Diego). If you want to visit Frida's house, do this
route in reverse and **buy tickets online as early as possible** — it's the one attraction in
the city that is always packed. This is a great Saturday activity: you'll see what a typical
Mexican family does on a weekend.

Have breakfast [here](https://goo.gl/maps/49ENEc16iya7i5TbA) (go to the left-side door — the
left restaurant is nicer for breakfast). Then stroll to the
[Bazar del Sábado](https://g.page/BazaarSabado?share) — THE place for high-quality Mexican
handicrafts (pricier, but much better quality). Then do this exact walk to Coyoacán:
<https://goo.gl/maps/rXbicz4t9hfDV7FG9>. The best churros in the city are shortly after the
start, [here](https://goo.gl/maps/nWstg7XZEWKfqwQ97). Stop along the way at the cultural centers
and coffee shops. At the end, sit on a bench in the park near the wolf fountain and watch
Mexican life in all its glory.

## Zona Condesa / Roma

Explore the neighborhood you're staying in — a stroll across the parks and plazas of Condesa
and Roma is a great way to spend a day. Sample walk: <https://goo.gl/maps/43qaiieQ2sMetGrq7>.

**Restaurants**

- Japanese (Kura): <https://g.page/izakayakura?share>
- Tasting menu that will ruin all other food for you — get a reservation (Lorea): <https://g.page/loreamx?share>
- Mexican-Yucateca, our go-to for a good meal without overpaying (La Capital): <https://goo.gl/maps/gxUFf6tSRfK7LhM96>
- Good tacos: Chetito; [El Parnita](https://elparnita.com/) during the day and Páramo at night; for street tacos try [El Güero](https://goo.gl/maps/2zgbDm6A5gxujmXK6) (bistek)
- Mediterranean: <https://goo.gl/maps/ZoY5mfQSheCaFTtY8>
- Good Mexican place: <https://goo.gl/maps/KGeR4xPN4KGduofr5>
- More good Mexican food: <https://goo.gl/maps/biX5hqbEF4uJN49b8>
- Ceviche / seafood: <https://goo.gl/maps/vFv21GDDgYPDAGL69>

**Taco stands**

- [El Comal Oculto](https://maps.app.goo.gl/JXS61fxXdKUv4HwZ6) — outstanding tacos, quesadillas, and all kinds of antojitos
- Hole-in-the-wall Arab-style tacos, our personal favorite: <https://goo.gl/maps/HPem8vz44HFoZovG7>
- <https://goo.gl/maps/GzDqGu88ZCopJnD48>
- [Taquería Álvaro Obregón](https://g.page/TaqueriaAlvaroO?share)

**Coffee shops & bakeries**

- [Saint](https://www.instagram.com/saintpanaderia/?hl=en) — great bread and coffee
- [Rosetta](https://g.page/panaderiarosetta?share) — great coffee, pastries, and bread
- [Tout Chocolat](https://goo.gl/maps/WfztHVT7dsyc6ZgaA)
- [Blend Station](https://g.page/BlendStation?share)
- El Péndulo — several locations: [one](https://goo.gl/maps/QhLZodqU7HkjZSGt8), [another](https://goo.gl/maps/fVmW7no2cHFXitas6)
- [Centro Galera](https://goo.gl/maps/Eb4Lu5CLYQFSFm2E7)

**Drinks**

- Really nice rooftop: <https://goo.gl/maps/BsTXGSJeBY1qeGx16>
- Great mezcal bar: <https://goo.gl/maps/bmJWw95iNYPYouPX7>
- Great mezcal bar #2: <https://goo.gl/maps/VBv7kwpgD5H5yCop6>
- Great pulque bar: <https://goo.gl/maps/NLiPKVBmcxQQZYeA7>

## Assorted tips

- On **Mondays** most museums and attractions are closed — a good day to visit **Teotihuacán**. Book a tour or just Uber there ([good drop-off spot](https://goo.gl/maps/vhasuP8zCwQCq1oz6)). Beyond the Pyramids of the Sun and Moon, stroll the museum and make the trek to the [Templo de Quetzalcóatl](https://goo.gl/maps/MrWzpHaj8m65Ekef8).
- For **Xochimilco**, no need to book ahead (unless you want a kayak tour or similar). [This is a good spot](https://goo.gl/maps/PASHZ4ZfcHo84E8W9) to Uber to; prices are posted and fixed.

## Outdoor activities

If you're an outdoor enthusiast, CDMX has a lot to offer — hiking, road and mountain biking,
and rock climbing. A few nearby hikes:

- **Desierto de los Leones** — lots of hiking and mountain biking (weekend MTB rental). [Good parking/trailhead](https://goo.gl/maps/uz7cwSWaxD8AYzyM9); the taco/quesadilla stand at the start is great — try the "Taco sin llorar".
- **Ajusco** — the tallest mountain within the city, in a protected alpine forest. Short but steep; great views on a clear day. We park [here](https://goo.gl/maps/1r7WZARHm4nGHB769) and hike from there.
- [This ejido](https://goo.gl/maps/uRCTFxiTRAbuwK3t7) has many hiking and mountain-biking trails.
- **Mount Tláloc** — a wonderful all-day hike, usually started from [Río Frío](https://goo.gl/maps/hvLskZQNVNyShMKFA). The summit has the ruins of an Aztec observatory.
- **Rock climbing**: [Los Dinamos](https://goo.gl/maps/iq8E7RL6YwVFQXA7A) (sport, trad, and bouldering), bouldering in [Salazar](https://goo.gl/maps/yS976EWMRfhMBLfA7), and great sport climbing in [Jilotepec](https://goo.gl/maps/rFczCMQeqTm891Kd9).
- Paso de Cortés.
